text:

Welcome, to project Mirei or rather known as the registry of institutional realism warbuilding project. This is a story writing, story building, worldbuilding, warbuilding, and also in overall to create a general ecosystem and a lived world, where the author partake in the world itself, traverses its logic, see it and create contents that of resemblance, or at least, internal to the world itself, similarly for now the details are, and how the construction of the world can be, alongside its stories. The philosophy around this is perspective realism, and institutional realism, most probable as to somewhat, in a sense and in hindsight to capture the realism of documentary, reports, incomplete and fragmented information, distorted presentation, rhetoric, the complexity and uncertainty of time and in time rather than the omniscience vantage point most authors utilizes to great effect, and of which the scale are overproportioned, and only presented matter-of-fact with padding and patches. Such is what there is, and thus, is what to be for the project itself.
Most of the time, the trilogy would track the human civilization that is taken of a very, very long period of times, starting from the concurrent modern histories segments, down from the first day of the Christian calendar, to the present time; and from there, sequences of events and historic rupture would take the calendar to reset to a new calendar. What entails such triviality, would be presented in the stories itself. For now, the main lensing would be focused on the human civilization and its perspective, as for us to live inside such civilization. We declare this as phase I of the warbuilding, and thus we can now start with it. However, it is not as if we cannot shift perspectives and POV into the other empires of such. However, in doing so, would be secondary, and what if the other object has no coherent thought?
As also implied by the conjectured terminology, warbuilding is also to refer to the art of building strategic warfiction, where warfiction is just fiction warfare and its nature being experimental. Specifically, a war is not of sensation, per the philosophy. Sensation, is built after the warcraft is perfected, its strategy cemented, fog of war clearly stated, system clearly crystallized, moments analyzed, and so on of the act to build the war itself down to intricate details, and the way people speak 1. In general, it is an experimental testbed, for formal, rigorous and often inconspicuously easy to miss scaffolding of war design, but then also for novel situations and scenarios to unfold correctly. Without or with info dumps, of course, and or not.
1 One of the gripe about this usually, is the lack of insulated voice design. That is, info-dumping, or breakage in deliverance, for a commanding officer of a field army suddenly feel like he has to yap about quantum computing fundamentals in an active scenario, or so. Or a bureaucratic leaders suddenly taking a leeway to yap about political theories that, usually those in his positions already faimilar with, to lecture the audience unwillingly. And also to specify everything, talk about everything, in an environment where everything must be obscured, again, like in military you teezer.





NoteAbout the term warbuilding terms



The term itself has been used extensively from the original blog post the warbuilding guide to interstellar warfare. In general, this is the statement thereof that born this term.

Star Trek, to Star Wars; from Battlestar Galactica, to sci-fi military world-building. From fictions to fictions, we have been trying to depict wars, depicting military structures, and depicting different kind of command structure, or institution. While stories of such, and their focus on the individuals, the actors, the heroes, and so on, are fantastic and spectacular, they fail in one certain aspect. The depiction of survival, the depiction of an organic system, the depiction of existence of a typical institution. The depiction at most, of constraints, within those parameters, without magic, without Deus ex machina, without god-giving grace. Boiling down to technical domain, everything simply sounds fake. Intents, personalities, individuals leakage in places where one expects actual order. Coldness in wrong tensor, personal in wrong consequence. Such is the failing grace of what can be observed from latent media or fictions of which we have seen, though one can forbid such incompleteness and focus on the things they did best - drawing out a world of fiction and stories related to the actors. But we want a different thing. So let us try doing that, this time, through a kind of story: The cold, hard, monotonic facet of reports.
